title: Three Family Members of Sepideh Gholian Arrested in Dezful
content:
According to HRANA, three members of Sepideh Gholian’s family were arrested in Dezful.

On Monday, November 16, 2026, security agents raided Ms. Gholian’s family home in Dezful. Finding her absent, they arrested her father, Khodarahm Gholian, and her 17-year-old niece, Tahoura, using violence and physical assault.

Mehdi Gholian, the civil rights activist’s brother, was also arrested by security agents when he went to inquire about the situation of his detained father and niece. He was subsequently transferred to Dezful Prison.

Sepideh Gholian has stated that security agents informed her family that her previously suspended five-year prison sentence, issued following her arrest at a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi in Mashhad, had been put into effect due to her recent interviews and human rights activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, three members of Sepideh Gholian’s family were arrested in Dezful.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Prisoner Executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed today at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged on the morning of Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as Hamid Karouni.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Karouni had previously been arrested on a murder charge and subsequently sentenced to death by judicial authorities.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRANA, 1,062 people were executed by hanging in Iran between January 1 and October 31, 2026, amid a sharp increase in executions over the past two years.
snippet: According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed today at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged on the morning of Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as Hamid Karouni.

title: Yazd Prison: Report on the Judicial Status of 28 Detainees Arrested During the January Protests
content:
As part of ongoing efforts to monitor and document the situation of individuals arrested during the nationwide protests of January 2026, this report sheds light on the legal cases and detention conditions of several prisoners held in Yazd Prison. In addition, this report provides details about the judicial proceedings against them, restrictions imposed on the prisoners and their families, and detention conditions in certain sections of the prison.

HRANA’s findings indicate that, among the 28 prisoners examined, 15 have been sentenced to prison terms ranging from three to 21 years, while the remaining 13 continue to face legal uncertainty months after their arrests. In the cases of several of these individuals, social media activity, publishing content, communicating with media outlets based outside Iran, and using communications equipment have been among the matters cited in judicial proceedings against them.

title: Baha’i Citizen Mobin Hosseini Arrested After Appearing at Sari Prosecutor’s Office
content:
According to HRANA, Mobin Hosseini, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested today, Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

Based on information received by HRANA, Hosseini attended an interrogation session today at the Sari Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office, where he defended himself against charges including “propaganda against the regime.” He was arrested following the conclusion of the session.

Hosseini had previously been arrested at his home on October 11, 2026, by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization, who reportedly beat him and took him into custody without presenting a judicial warrant. He was released several hours later. During the incident, the agents also verbally and physically assaulted him and confiscated his mobile phone.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding any additional charges that may have been brought against Mobin Hosseini or his current place of detention.
snippet: According to HRANA, Mobin Hosseini, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested today, Tuesday, November 17, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Kurdistan Province: Nine Suspects Arrested by Ministry of Intelligence Agents on Security-Related Charges
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mehr News Agency, the Ministry of Intelligence announced in a statement that it had arrested nine individuals on security-related charges in Kurdistan Province.

According to the statement, the detainees are accused of “membership in separatist groups and organizing armed activities aimed at creating insecurity in Kurdistan Province.”

The Ministry of Intelligence also announced the arrest of a key leader of these groups who, according to the ministry, had been residing abroad. The statement alleged that the individual, acting under the direction of a regional intelligence service, was responsible for establishing and leading an armed network in Kamyaran County.

The statement further claimed that firearms and 70 Starlink communication devices had been discovered and confiscated from the suspects.

The ministry’s statement did not disclose the identities of those arrested, the exact dates of their arrests, or their current places of detention.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mehr News Agency, the Ministry of Intelligence announced in a statement that it had arrested nine individuals on security-related charges in Kurdistan Province.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence Against Defendant in Rasht
content:
According to HRANA, citing Tasnim News Agency, the judiciary spokesperson announced that Branch 39 of the Supreme Court has upheld a death sentence against a defendant.

Without disclosing the defendant’s identity, Seyed Ali Kazemi alleged that the individual was involved in attacks on eight locations in Rasht, including Imam Sajjad Clinic, Refah and Sepah banks, Quds Mosque, the Gilan Provincial Department of Education, the Iran Insurance building, and the Rasht Civil Court. According to Kazemi, a nurse named Marzieh Nabi-Nia lost her life in the fire at Imam Sajjad Clinic.

The judiciary spokesperson stated that the defendant had been sentenced to death and that Branch 39 of the Supreme Court upheld the ruling in October-November 2026.

He further alleged that the defendant, along with two other individuals, had prepared and stored a large number of Molotov cocktails and incendiary materials in the basement of a residential building in Rasht at least 10 days before January 8, 2026.

Regarding the circumstances of the arrest, Kazemi stated that Basij forces apprehended the defendant while he was allegedly attempting to attack a mosque.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Tasnim News Agency, the judiciary spokesperson announced that Branch 39 of the Supreme Court has upheld a death sentence against a defendant.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Semnan: Three Baha’i Citizens Arrested, Homes of Five Families Searched by Intelligence Agents
content:
According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 15, 2026, intelligence agents searched the homes of five Baha’i families in Semnan and arrested three individuals.

Based on information received by HRANA, agents of the Ministry of Intelligence stopped Behfar Khanjani while he was traveling, physically assaulted him, handcuffed him, and took him to his residence. The agents searched his family home and arrested him. The search lasted six hours.

According to relatives of the family, Khanjani’s daughter, who was home alone when the agents suddenly entered, was severely frightened. During the search, agents confiscated the mobile phones belonging to Khanjani and his wife, along with laptops found in the residence.

In another incident, agents searched the home of Hesam Tabianian and his wife, Zohreh Nik-Ayin, and arrested both of them. The couple’s mobile phones and a laptop were confiscated. Agents also searched Tabianian’s shop and his mother’s residence.
snippet: According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 15, 2026, intelligence agents searched the homes of five Baha’i families in Semnan and arrested three individuals.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Appeals Court Upholds Prison Sentence Against Baha’i Citizen Arman Misaghian
content:
According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Arman Misaghian has been upheld in full on appeal.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 21 of the Tehran Province Court of Appeals upheld Misaghian’s sentence of one year in prison for the charge of “propaganda against the regime” and an additional year for “insulting the Supreme Leader.”

The court also upheld supplementary penalties prohibiting the Baha’i citizen from driving, signing commercial documents, and participating in groups for a period of two years.

The ruling was communicated to Arman Misaghian late last week.

Misaghian had previously received the same sentence in the initial proceedings before Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Seyed Ali Mazloum.

No information has been obtained regarding the specific acts or evidence underlying the charges brought against this Baha’i citizen.
snippet: According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Arman Misaghian has been upheld in full on appeal.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Supreme Court Rejects Appeal of Imprisoned Lawyer Javad Alikordi
content:
According to HRANA, the Supreme Court has rejected Javad Alikordi’s appeal.

Abbas Mousavi, Mr. Alikordi’s defense attorney, announced in a statement that the Supreme Court had rejected his client’s request for a retrial and upheld his sentences, including imprisonment, internal exile, permanent disbarment from practicing law, and a travel ban.

Mr. Mousavi further stated: “The only remaining opportunity to avoid or reduce these severe punishments is to request a retrial under Article 474 of the Criminal Procedure Code, provided that the legal grounds for such a request are met.”

In June of this year, Javad Alikordi was sentenced by Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court to five years in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion to act against national security” and 13 years in prison on the charge of “propaganda activities against national security.” The court also sentenced him to permanent disbarment from practicing law, a two-year travel ban, and two years of internal exile in Sistan and Baluchestan Province.

On June 10, 2026, a court hearing addressing the charges against Mr. Alikordi was held at Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court.
snippet: According to HRANA, the Supreme Court has rejected Javad Alikordi’s appeal.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Hossein Rasouli-Nasab’s Death Sentence Commuted to Prison Term
content:
According to HRANA, Hossein Rasouli-Nasab’s death sentence has been commuted to imprisonment. Relatives of Mr. Rasouli-Nasab announced on social media that his death sentence had been commuted to a prison term following the application of a pardon and a one-degree reduction in his punishment.

HRANA is working to verify the exact length of his new prison sentence.

His death sentence had previously been upheld by the Supreme Court, and his case had been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Unit.

Hossein Rasouli-Nasab was sentenced to death in a joint case alongside Mehdi Zarif, Matin Shabani, Hassan Golshan-Nejad, Ali Zaghi, and Iliya Akbari by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge.

The charges brought against the defendants in this case included “moharebeh (enmity against God) through participation in the destruction of public property and the setting fire to religious centers” and “assembly and collusion against national security.”

title: Nazanin Abedini, a Baha’i Citizen, Sentenced to Prison and Deprivation of Social Rights
content:
According to HRANA, Nazanin Abedini Kafshgari has been sentenced to imprisonment and deprivation of social rights.

According to a verdict issued on November 10, 2026, by Branch 1 of the Sari Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Ammar Ramezani, Ms. Abedini was sentenced to three years in prison and eight years of deprivation of social rights.

In this case, Ms. Abedini faced charges of “propaganda against the Islamic Republic” and “propaganda in favor of groups or organizations opposed to the Islamic Republic of Iran.” However, in its ruling, the court classified her educational and religious activities, including teaching Baha’i beliefs to children and engaging in online activities, as falling under Paragraph 2 of Article 500 bis of the Islamic Penal Code, and issued its verdict on that basis.

According to the verdict, reports from the Ministry of Intelligence offices in Qaem Shahr, Juybar, and Simorgh, along with the contents of her mobile phone, photographs, texts, and educational materials, were among the evidence cited by the court in issuing the sentence.
snippet: According to HRANA, Nazanin Abedini Kafshgari has been sentenced to imprisonment and deprivation of social rights.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Female Prisoner Executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, a female prisoner was executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn yesterda, Sunday, November 15, as Fatemeh Farhadi.

Based on information received by HRANA, Ms. Farhadi had previously been arrested on non-political charges and was subsequently sentenced to death by the relevant judicial authority.

As of the time of this report, the execution of this female prisoner has not been announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRANA, 1,062 people were executed by hanging in Iran between January 1 and October 31, 2026, amid a sharp increase in executions over the past two years.

title: Fariba Asadi Sentenced to Six Years in Prison and Additional Penalties
content:
According to HRANA, Fariba Asadi has been sentenced to imprisonment and other penalties.

Based on information received by HRANA, Ms. Asadi was sentenced to six years in prison on charges of “assembly and collusion, acting against national security, and participating in protests.”

Additionally, as supplementary punishment, the court imposed a two-year ban on leaving the country, membership in social groups and organizations, and employment in government and public-sector positions.

The court hearing to address the charges against Fariba Asadi was held on September 7, 2026, at Branch 2 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Sabzevari.

Fariba Asadi, a civil rights activist residing in Karaj, was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents on January 26, 2026. She was subsequently transferred to Kachooei Prison in Karaj and released on bail of three billion tomans after approximately three months in detention.

Ms. Asadi has previously faced judicial proceedings and arrest in connection with her activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Fariba Asadi has been sentenced to imprisonment and other penalties.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison, Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of one of the prisoners as Morteza Naghdi, 30.

Based on information received by HRANA, Mr. Naghdi had previously been arrested on a murder charge and sentenced to death by a criminal court. Prior to his execution, he was held in Ward 7 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

Earlier, Mizan, the judiciary’s official news agency, reported the execution of a prisoner without disclosing his identity. HRANA has identified the prisoner as Saeed Amel.

According to Mizan, he had been sentenced to death on charges of murder and rape.

At the time of this report, the execution of Morteza Naghdi had not been announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

According to HRANA, 1,062 people were executed by hanging in Iran between January 1 and October 31, 2026, amid a sharp increase in executions over the past two years.

title: Three More Detainees from the January 2026 Protests Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari have been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, the three individuals were sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Among the charges brought against them is allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel. The death sentences were communicated to the three individuals in October 2026.

The three men were arrested by security forces in January 2026 in connection with the nationwide protests. Following their arrests, they were transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison, where they remained for some time.

During the summer of 2026, Hossein Parvin, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari were transferred from the Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, where they have remained incarcerated ever since.

HRANA’s investigation into the specific allegations underlying the charges against these three individuals is ongoing.

Background: The January 2026 Protests
snippet: According to HRANA, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari have been sentenced to death.

title: At Least Six Arrested During Protest in Abdanan
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, six individuals were arrested during protests in Abdanan.

Today, three of those arrested were identified as Sina Darvishi, a 15-year-old teenager, Asghar Akbari, and Armin Soleimani. The arrests of Iraj Heydari, Saeed Abdollahi, and Behnam Moradi had also been reported yesterday.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the detainees’ whereabouts, conditions, or the charges brought against them.

Yesterday afternoon, hundreds of residents gathered in Abdanan to protest the deaths of 13 people in the bus rollover accident involving employees of the Dehloran Petrorefinery Complex. Chanting slogans against government officials, protesters expressed outrage over poor road conditions, inadequate infrastructure, and mismanagement. In solidarity with the protesters and the victims’ families, some businesses in the city’s bazaar also went on strike.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, six individuals were arrested during protests in Abdanan.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency
